questions.stem: Choose the correct option regarding the storage temperatures of blood components.
questions.solutionHtml:
The recommended storage temperatures of different blood components is as follows:

Blood component Storage temperature
Whole blood and red blood cells 2–6°C
Fresh frozen plasma -30°C or lower
Cryoprecipitate Below -30°C

Albumin

Freeze-dried factor VIII

 2–8°C
Platelet 20–24°C

 





Online Resource, http://www.who.int/bloodsafety/Manual_on_Management,Maintenance_and_Use_of_Blood_Cold_Chain_Equipment.pdf Page 5
Online Resource, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4260297/#:~:text=As%20per%20standard%20guidelines%5B22,%2C%20below%20%E2%88%9218%C2%B0C.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be used to store blood for up to 35 days?
questions.solutionHtml:
Citrate dextrose phosphate adenine-1 (CDPA-1) can be used to store blood for up to 35 days. It helps in improving ATP synthesis during storage. Hence, it increases the shelf life.

The disadvantage of using CDPA-1 is that it increases uric acid stone formation.

The shelf life of storage with other components are:

  • Acid Citrate dextrose – 21 days
  • Citrate-phosphate dextrose – 21 days




Journal, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/7222197
Wintrobe’s Clinical Hematology 13th Edition, Page no 550
Online Resource, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/6710583

questions.stem: What is correct regarding transfusion of the blood received from blood bank?

options.label: A
options.text: It should be started within 4 hours of receiving it from the blood bank.

options.label: B
options.text: It should be completed within 4 hours of receiving from the blood bank.

options.label: C
options.text: No such time restraint and can be done anytime.

options.label: D
options.text: It should be completed within 6 hours of receiving from the blood bank.

questions.answerText: It should be completed within 4 hours of receiving from the blood bank.
questions.solutionHtml:
Blood received from blood bank should be completely transfused within 4 hours of receiving.

Principles of blood administration:

  • All blood products should be given through an appropriate blood administration set containing a filter.
  • A careful aseptic technique should be practised at all times.
  • Vital signs should be documented before and after transfusion and as clinically required. For the first 15 minutes after the infusion has begun, the patient should be kept under close observation to detect any signs of a serious transfusion reaction. If none is observed, the infusion rate may be increased.
  • One unit of red cells is often given in 1 to 4 hours, depending on the amount to be transfused and on the patient’s cardiovascular status. Infusion of a unit for longer than 4 hours is not recommended, as there is a risk of bacterial proliferation because the opened unit is at room temperature.
  • No other solution and no medication should be added to or infused through the same tubing as a blood product.
  • Ringer’s lactate or other solutions containing calcium must never be added to a blood product because the calcium present leads to coagulation.
  • After the transfusion has been completed, the transfusion tag or record should become part of the patient’s chart.




Wintrobe's Clinical Hematology, 11th Edition, Page no 565

questions.stem: Which of the following patients receiving blood transfusions are more prone to develop bacterial sepsis?

options.label: A
options.text: A young women with severe anaemia

questions.solutionHtml:
Patients with thrombocytopenia receiving blood transfusions (platelets) are more prone to develop bacterial sepsis. 

Sepsis is mostly due to significant bacterial contamination of the blood products. Platelets have the maximum risk of causing this condition when compared to red cell preparations. Since patients with thrombocytopenia receive platelet transfusion, they are at an increased risk of infections.

Platelets (unlike red cells) must be stored at room temperature. This is a condition that is favourable for bacterial proliferation. Broad-spectrum antibiotics must be started while waiting for the culture reports.

The blood components that are preferred for the other conditions are:

  • Anaemia - RBCs
  • Hemophilia - FFP
  • vonWillebrand disease - cryoprecipitate




Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9e, page no. 666

questions.stem: A patient has been brought with severe bleeding to your ER. His blood group is unknown. Fresh frozen plasma from which of the following blood groups can be given?
questions.solutionHtml:
Fresh Frozen Plasma (FFP) from AB blood group can be given to this patient as it is the universal plasma donor. AB plasma does not contain antibodies against antigens on RBCs of AB blood group.

O Rh-negative blood is the universal blood donor. It is used during emergency packed cell blood transfusion with an unknown blood group. It is preferred because it lacks the A and B and Rh antigens. Hence, it cannot be hemolyzed by anti-A, anti-B or anti-D antibodies in the recipient’s blood.





Miller's Anesthesia 8th edition, Page nos 1840 and 1841
Online Resource, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4469576/
Miller's Anesthesia 9th edition, Page no: 1547

questions.stem: What is the most common reaction occurring in patients undergoing blood transfusions?
questions.solutionHtml:
The most common blood transfusion reaction is the febrile nonhemolytic reaction.





Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9e, Page no: 665

questions.stem: Blood transfusion was started in a patient with severe anaemia. Within a few minutes she developed generalised pruritis, swelling of the tongue and stridor. Which antibody deficiency in the recipient most commonly causes this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
The given clinical scenario is suggestive of severe, potentially fatal, allergic reactions. These are most likely to occur in patients with IgA deficiency.

Such reactions may occur when blood products containing certain antigens are given to previously sensitized recipients. It is triggered by recipient IgG antibodies that recognize IgA in the infused blood product.





Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10e, Page no: 671

questions.stemHtml: Following blood transfusion in a post-operative patient, the following finding was noted. Which of the following is responsible for this reaction?
questions.solutionHtml:
The given image, showing a raised and erythematous lesion, is suggestive of urticaria. Such reactions may be triggered by the presence of an allergen in the donated blood product that is recognized by IgE antibodies in the recipient.

These are mild reactions occurring more commonly in 1% to 3% of transfusions.





Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9e, page no. 665

questions.stem: A patient with thalassemia developed pallor and dizziness 1 week following blood transfusion. His lab reports are given below. Which of the following is seen in this condition?

options.label: A
options.text: Direct coombs test negative, IgG mediated

options.label: B
options.text: Direct Coombs test positive, IgG mediated

options.label: C
options.text: Direct coombs test negative, IgM mediated

options.label: D
options.text: Direct coombs test positive, IgM mediated

questions.answerText: Direct Coombs test positive, IgG mediated
questions.solutionHtml:
The given clinical scenario is suggestive of delayed hemolytic reaction following blood transfusion. It is IgG mediated and gives a positive result in direct Coombs test.

These antibodies recognize foreign protein red cell antigens in a previously sensitized recipient (through a prior blood transfusion). They present with laboratory features of hemolysis like low haptoglobin level and elevated LDH.

Acute hemolytic reactions are usually caused by preformed IgM antibodies against donor red cells that fix complement. The direct Coombs test is usually positive. 






Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9e, page no. 666

questions.stem: A patient who was admitted for blood transfusion developed transfusion-related acute lung injury. Which of the following statements is false about this condition?

options.label: A
options.text: Pre-existing lung diseases are a risk factor

options.label: B
options.text: Incidence with platelet transfusion is more than that with whole blood

options.label: C
options.text: Symptoms develop after 2 days of transfusion

options.label: D
options.text: Subsequent transfusions from the same donor increases the incidence

questions.answerText: Symptoms develop after 2 days of transfusion
questions.solutionHtml:
Transfusion-related acute lung injury (TRALI) is sudden-onset respiratory failure that occurs during or soon after the transfusion. It occurs within 6 hours, and not after 2 days following transfusion.

TRALI is a severe fatal complication of blood transfusion. The incidence of TRALI is low (1 per 10,000 transfusions). However, it may occur more frequently in patients with preexisting lung disease.  

The pathogenesis involves a two-hit hypothesis:

  • Priming event - increased sequestration and sensitization of neutrophils in the microvasculature of the lung
  • Second hit - the factor (most commonly MHC class I antigens) present in the transfused blood product activates the primed neutrophils

TRALI can occur in transfusions with all plasma-containing blood products. However, it is more likely to occur following the transfusion of fresh frozen plasma and platelets. This is because these products contain high levels of donor antibodies.  

Note: TRALI is important to recognize because donor products that induce complications in one patient are much more likely to do so in a second. Indeed, recent measures to exclude multiparous women from plasma donation have resulted in reduced incidence of TRALI.





Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9e, Page no 666

questions.stem: A 33-year-old man is receiving massive blood transfusion following a fall from height. 4 hours after transfusion, he becomes breathless and oxygen saturation decreases. Chest X-ray shows diffuse bilateral lung infiltrates. Which of the following statements is false regarding this condition?

options.label: B
options.text: Treatment involves discontinuation of blood transfusion

options.label: D
options.text: It is mediated by macrophages in lung vasculature

questions.answerText: It is mediated by macrophages in lung vasculature
questions.solutionHtml:
The given clinical scenario is suggestive of TRALI (transfusion-related acute lung injury). It is mediated by neutrophils entrapped in the lung vasculature.

Features of TRALI are:

  • Fever
  • Hypotension
  • Hypoxemia
  • Bilateral pulmonary infiltrates - not responsive to diuretics

Treatment is mainly supportive and blood transfusions are discontinued. The mortality rate in this condition is 5-10%.





Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9e, Page no 666
Online Resource, https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/agricultural-and-biological-sciences/transfusion-related-acute-lung-injury

questions.stem: A CKD patient had to undergo dialysis and his Hb was 5.2gm/dL. So two blood transfusions were to be given. The first bag was completed in 2 hours. The second was started and in the midway, he developed shortness of breath and hypertension. Vitals were BP - 180/120 mmHg and pulse rate - 110/min. What is the cause?
questions.solutionHtml:
The given clinical scenario is suggestive of transfusion-associated circulatory overload (TACO). 

TACO is caused by rapid or excess transfusion of red cell preparations or plasma products. This condition is characterized by:

  • Dyspnea with O2% <90 at room air
  • Bilateral infiltrates on chest X-ray
  • Systolic hypertension
  • Elevation of brain natriuretic peptide, 1.5 times that of pre-transfusion levels

It can be prevented by administering the transfusion slowly, at the rate of 1 to 2 ml of blood/kg of body weight per hour. Diuretics are also used if necessary. 





Wintrobe’s Clinical Hematology 13th Edition, Page no 576
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 20th Edition, Page no 814

questions.stem: A patient who receives recurrent transfusions for thalassemia develops fever and chills during this time. There is no evidence of hemolysis. Which of the following measures can decrease the rate of transfusion reactions?
questions.solutionHtml:
The given scenario is suggestive of febrile non-hemolytic transfusion reaction (FNHTR). Such reactions can be prevented by using leukoreduced RBCs.
Removal of leukocytes from the blood is called leukoreduction. It is done before storage to prevent cytokine formation.
FNHTR may occur due to the following:
  • Sensitization to the WBC antigens by previous blood transfusions or pregnancy
  • Cytokines produced by the donor leukocytes during storage
  • Bacterial contamination

Note: Luspatercept is an erythroid maturation agent, a receptor fusion protein consisting of a modified extracellular domain of human activin receptor type-2B linked to the human Ig-G1 Fc domain. The drug was recently approved by the FDA for the treatment of transfusion-dependent thalassemia.





Wintrobe’s Clinical Hematology 13th Edition, Page nos 574 and 575
